related_resources.reason: Damped normal equations and historical orientation.

authorship.scope: Original standalone mathematical exposition, exact equations, worked examples and exercises for the nonlinear least-squares and inverse-problem bridge; inherited manuscripts preserved.

prerequisites.reason: Local convergence and why globalization matters.

recommended.reason: QR and numerically stable augmented least squares.

background: Least squares and Jacobians, positive-definite matrices and elementary Lagrange multipliers.
readiness_checks: Can you explain why a local descent direction need not produce descent with a full step?
Can you derive a stationarity equation after adding a quadratic penalty to a step?

description: Shows why a plausible Gauss–Newton direction can fail, derive damped steps and trust-region acceptance, and distinguish step control from changing the fitted objective.
